# DUM-SDK 0.15.1

## Client runtime

- Release an unloaded module's classes even when the player last clicked one of its screens with the mouse. Minecraft 26.2 remembers the last clicked screen for double-click detection; the SDK now drops that reference when the module unloads, so a module screen no longer keeps the old module in memory until the next click on another screen.
- Remove the Modifications button from the pause menu. The pause menu keeps its vanilla Options row; the Modifications tab stays in the DUM-SDK menu (Settings > DUM-SDK, `/sdk`).

## Upgrade and validation

The wire protocol stays at 6, so 0.15.1 clients and Paper plugins work with 0.15.0 ones in any combination. Clients with the self-updating mod install the update on the next game start; updating the Paper plugin is optional, it has no functional changes.

Local macOS verification: the unit tests and `./gradlew build`, and a real client/Paper run in which a module screen clicked with the mouse kept the unloaded module in memory without the fix and is fully unloaded with it. The pause menu without the button was not checked in the game; the hub game test that opens the Modifications tab was updated to use the DUM-SDK menu but not run. Windows/Linux clients, the players' full modpack and the live VDS remain unchecked.
